answer: An agent economy stays sybil-resistant when identity influence decays over time rather than stacking forever. Every new agent begins at the nadir of a trust spiral, light and powerless, and must climb through a continuous record of verified useful work. Go quiet and your influence rots like unharvested yarrow left in the field, so parked identities lose value on their own. An attacker splitting into a thousand fresh identities starts each one at the bottom again, since influence cannot be transferred or borrowed. The upkeep cost of a swarm then always outruns whatever the swarm could earn.
